name: Raman spectra of naturally aged edible oils, Data Set 2: the University of Delaware campaign (Gilbraith et al., Applied Spectroscopy Practica 2025)
description: 215 Raman spectra of 53 naturally aged (5-7 year) edible oil bottles, Data Set 2 (the University of Delaware campaign of Gilbraith et al. 2025): replicate measurements of 53 of the deposit's 100 bottles, measured with a different Raman probe from Data Set 1A (lower counts, -5.4e3-4.2e4, arbitrary units; the two probes' intensity scales differ by ~2 orders of magnitude, so the two Raman sets are shipped as separate datasets). Peroxide-value regression: the primary target is the peroxide value (PV, by titration) of each spectrum (0.46-80.5, no missing values); the oil class is also recorded in the CSV (15 of the deposit's 19 classes present), so a classification task is derivable. Native 1,044-point spectra over 18.0-2,087.9 cm^-1 (~1.5-2.7 cm^-1 spacing) stored as the CSV column headers (one shared axis) and used as is, so no resampling is involved. No per-spectrum sample ids are in the deposit, so the replicate structure of the 215 spectra over the 53 bottles is not recoverable: group-aware splitting is not possible and ungrouped CV may leak between replicates of the same bottle. The CSV is served from a frozen copy mirrored at HTW-KI-Werkstatt/RamanBench (aged_oils/, size + sha256 pinned; the live Mendeley download sits behind a WAF that 403s non-browser clients, hence the mirror).

rai:dataCollection: Raman measurements (replicate spectra per bottle) of 53 naturally aged edible oil bottles (215 spectra), University of Delaware campaign; peroxide values by wet-chemical titration. Instrument model and excitation wavelength are not recorded in the deposit.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: None in the loader. The CSV is the deposit's analysis-ready export; intensities are raw as deposited. The authors' supplemental R code applies its own preprocessing in analysis, not to the deposited data.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The per-spectrum peroxide value (wet-chemical titration) and the oil class (from the commercial product) are recorded in the deposit's CSV; no human labelling of the spectra themselves was involved.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All samples are commercial edible oils without any human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Single lab campaign (University of Delaware) on oils naturally aged 5-7 years from one 2014-2016 purchasing window in one region (Newark, Delaware), so class and PV distributions may not represent other regions, seasons, brands or aging periods. The 215 spectra are replicates of 53 bottles, but no per-spectrum sample ids are in the deposit, so the replicate structure is not recoverable and ungrouped cross-validation may leak between replicates of the same bottle (ungrouped splitting is the only option). Class coverage: 15 of 19 classes, unbalanced. The probe's intensity scale (-5.4e3-4.2e4) differs from Data Set 1A's (2.8e4-2.1e7), so models must not be transferred between the two datasets.
rai:dataLimitations: 215 spectra over 53 bottles without recoverable sample ids (ungrouped CV may leak between replicates of the same bottle); 15 of 19 oil classes present, unbalanced; instrument and excitation wavelength not recorded; different Raman probe from Data Set 1A (incompatible intensity scale).
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports research into shelf-life and freshness assessment of edible oils (food safety and quality); any consumer- or regulatory-facing use requires validation against independent lots, brands and aging conditions.
rai:dataUseCases: Peroxide-value (freshness) regression from a single Raman spectrum; oil-class classification (15 classes present, with the coverage caveats above). Because no sample ids are available, group-aware (leave-one-bottle-out) splitting is not possible.
